I am an old woman now, eighty-five years, and my small piece of land near Mwanza is all I have left to work. My children help me when they can, but mostly I do what my late husband and I always did — I plant what I know, mix my crops together so if one fails another feeds me, and I save my little money for salt, soap, and the grandchildren. I cannot walk far to the agro-dealer, and one bag of fertilizer costs more shillings than I see in many months, so I just use the droppings from my few chickens and goats on the soil. I keep my own seeds from last harvest like my mother taught me, and I weed slowly with my hoe when my back allows.
